name: Fade In
tagline: Desktop screenwriting app that handles industry-standard script formatting, revisions and production paperwork.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Sold as a perpetual license rather than a subscription, so a monthly figure does not apply.

verdictSummary: Screenplay formatting is a solved, documented problem: Fountain gives you the markup, Courier Prime gives you the metrics, and an agent can wire up a live-formatted editor with page breaks and PDF export in a session. What you will not get in one shot is the boring half that working writers actually rely on: page-accurate pagination that matches what a line producer expects, Final Draft FDX round-tripping, revision modes with colored pages and asterisks, scene numbering locks, dual dialogue, and index card reordering. If you write for yourself and export PDFs for readers, the DIY version is genuinely fine. If anyone downstream opens your file in Final Draft or hands it to a production office, the interchange format is the whole job. It is a one-time license, not a subscription, which makes the payback math on building your own much less flattering.
coreLoopDIY: A local Fountain editor that live-formats as you type, paginates to standard screenplay metrics, and exports a clean PDF and title page.
requirements: Courier Prime font installed or bundled
Willingness to store scripts as plain .fountain files on disk
whatYouLose: FDX import and export, so no clean handoff to anyone on Final Draft
Production features: revision colors, asterisk marks, locked scene numbers, A/B pages
Page counts you can actually trust for scheduling and budgeting
Mobile and tablet apps, plus sync between machines
Outline and index card views, dual dialogue, and the thousand small formatting edge cases someone already fixed
moatNotes: The real lock is file format compatibility with Final Draft and the expectations of production offices, not the editor itself.
whyPeopleStillPay: It is a modest one-time price for software that already knows every formatting rule you would otherwise discover the hard way, at 2am, from a reader who says your script looks wrong. Fade In also reads and writes the formats the rest of the industry uses, which matters the moment a script leaves your laptop. A personal build is a lovely writing environment and a terrible interchange tool, and screenwriting is a collaborative business whether you like it or not.
notes: Fountain plus a print stylesheet gets you 80 percent of a screenwriting app in an afternoon; the last 20 percent is production paperwork nobody enjoys reimplementing.
prompt:
Build a local, offline screenwriting app in an empty folder. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry, no analytics.

Stack, non negotiable: Vite + React + TypeScript, plain CSS, no UI framework. Everything runs with `npm install && npm run dev`. No backend.

Core behavior:
- Two pane layout: a plain text editor on the left holding Fountain markup, a live formatted screenplay preview on the right.
- Parse Fountain yourself in a small module: scene headings (INT./EXT. or a leading dot), action, character cues, parentheticals, dialogue, transitions (to CUT TO: style or a leading gt marker), centered text, page breaks (===), notes in double brackets, and title page key/value block.
- Render the preview with real screenplay metrics: 12pt Courier Prime, 1 inch top and bottom, 1.5 inch left, 1 inch right, dialogue and character indents per standard, US Letter pages shown as discrete white sheets on a grey background.
- Paginate the preview into pages, never orphan a character cue at a page bottom, and add (MORE) plus (CONT'D) when dialogue splits across a page.
- Live stats bar: page count, scene count, word count.
- Scene navigator list built from scene headings; clicking one scrolls the preview.
- Character name autocomplete in the editor after a blank line when typing uppercase.

Files and export:
- Open and save .fountain files using the File System Access API, falling back to download and file input.
- Autosave the working draft to localStorage every few seconds and restore on load.
- Export PDF via a dedicated print stylesheet and window.print(), including an optional title page.

Explicitly out of scope, do not attempt: FDX or Final Draft import/export, revision colors and asterisks, locked scene numbers, index cards, collaboration, sync, mobile apps.

Bundle Courier Prime locally under /public/fonts. Ship a README with the supported Fountain syntax and a sample five page script in /examples so the app has something to show on first run.
